userdoc.notice: A creator-configured tax token that trades on a Uniswap v3 pool.

logo().notice: The token's artwork, as a URI. Empty when the creator supplied none.

owner().notice: The creator. May only ever call {reduceTaxes} and {renounce}.

portal().notice: The Argus Portal: launches the token, runs the bonding curve, and         performs the graduation LP mint. Tax-exempt.

graduate().notice: Flip on post-graduation behaviour: token-level tax, DEX trading,         and {swapBack}.

mainPool().notice: The v3 pool this token taxes against. Registered by the Portal at         LAUNCH (the address is CREATE2-deterministic), long before         {graduate} flips trading on, so the pre-graduation block below has         something real to block.

renounce().notice: Burn ownership. There is no other owner function besides         {reduceTaxes}: no pause, no blacklist, no mint, no wallet change.

swapBack().notice: Swap the accumulated tax tokens for native USDC and forward them         to the processor, minus a caller bounty.

graduated().notice: False while the token is on the bonding curve. Token-level tax         only runs after this flips; before it, the Portal charges the tax         in native at trade time.

taxExpiry().notice: `launchedAt + taxDuration`, or 0 when the tax is permanent. Can         never be re-armed or extended.

currentTaxes().notice: Effective rates right now: both read 0 once the tax has expired.

accumulatedTax().notice: Tokens currently waiting to be swapped back.

minSwapBackTokens().notice: Dust guard under the quote-value trigger, in tokens. Fixed at         launch; see {ArgusConstants-MIN_SWAPBACK_SUPPLY_DIVISOR} for why it is         set far below anything that can bind honestly.

swapBackThreshold().notice: The amount of accumulated tax, in TOKENS, that triggers a         swap-back right now.

setMainPool(address).notice: Register the canonical v3 pool. Called at LAUNCH, not graduation.

swapBack(uint256,uint256).notice: {swapBack}, with the caller choosing an upper bound on the slice.

reduceTaxes(uint16,uint16).notice: Down-only. Reverts if either argument exceeds the current value.

initialize((string,string,string,uint256.notice: One-shot setup, called by the factory in the same transaction as         `Clones.clone()`.

devdoc.details: Extends OpenZeppelin's {ERC20} DIRECTLY, and that is load-bearing. An      earlier token in this codebase (`HigherToken`) inserted itself into a      three-deep inheritance chain and its `_update` override became a silent      no-op, because `super._update` resolved to the sibling base rather than      to ERC20. Nothing reverted; the tax simply never moved. One base, one      unambiguous `super`.      Nothing here is `immutable`. This is an EIP-1167 clone target, and an      `immutable` is baked into the IMPLEMENTATION's runtime code, so every      clone would silently read the implementation's value - the same tax      rate, the same creator wallet, on every launch. All config lives in      storage, written once by {initialize}.      ONE KNOWN AND DELIBERATE DEPARTURE FROM ERC-20, stated here because an      integrator reads the contract header and not the middle of `_update`.      A sell debits the seller MORE than the amount passed to      `transferFrom`:          transferFrom(from, pool, value)  moves  value * (1 + sellTaxBps/1e4)          out of `from`, while spending allowance for `value` only.      The direction is the surprising part. An ordinary fee-on-transfer token      debits `value` and delivers less; this one delivers exactly `value`,      because a v3 pool re-reads its own balance and reverts if short by a      wei, and takes the tax as a surcharge from what the seller has left.      Approve `value * (1 + sellTaxBps/1e4)`, and do not infer the transferred      amount from a balance delta.      Charging the allowance for the surcharge would close the gap and would      make an exact-allowance sell revert, which is the honeypot signature the      surcharge exists to avoid. The gap is documented rather than moved. See      the note at the sell branch in {_update} for the full argument, and      audit finding M-1, 2026-09-03.

logo().details: THE NAME IS THE FEATURE. `logo()` is selector `0xfb7f21eb`, and that      is the first thing block explorers, wallets and our own token index      (`tools/arc-tokens.mjs`, which probes `logo()`, then `tokenURI()`,      then `metadataURI()`) staticcall when they want art for an Arc token.      A token that only emits its image in a launch event is discoverable      by exactly one indexer - ours, and only because we wrote it. Renaming      this getter makes the token render as a blank monogram everywhere.      No setter, deliberately, like everything else fixed at launch here.      Art that can be swapped after the fact is a rug vector: a token can      be sold under one image and re-skinned into another once it holds a      market. What the launch event says and what the getter says can      therefore never diverge.      There is no `tokenURI()` alongside this. See {ArgusPortal-TokenMeta}.

name().details: ERC20's `_name`/`_symbol` are written by ITS constructor, which never      runs for a clone - a clone would report the implementation's empty      strings. These read our own storage instead.

symbol().details: Returns the symbol of the token, usually a shorter version of the name.

decimals().details: Returns the number of decimals used to get its user representation. For example, if `decimals` equals `2`, a balance of `505` tokens should be displayed to a user as `5.05` (`505 / 10 ** 2`). Tokens usually opt for a value of 18, imitating the relationship between Ether and Wei. This is the default value returned by this function, unless it's overridden. NOTE: This information is only used for _display_ purposes: it in no way affects any of the arithmetic of the contract, including {IERC20-balanceOf} and {IERC20-transfer}.

graduate().details: Separate from {setMainPool} so the pre-graduation pool block has a      registered pool to enforce against for the whole curve phase.

swapBack().details: Deliberately a SEPARATE TRANSACTION, never reachable from      `_transfer`. On a v3 pool a taxed transfer runs *inside*      `pool.swap()` while the pool's reentrancy lock is held, so any      attempt to swap through that same pool from a transfer hook reverts.      This is the single hardest constraint in the design.      Sells ONLY the tax accumulator held at `balanceOf(address(this))`.      The graduation LP position is locked in the locker and is never      touched by anything here.

constructor.details: Locks the implementation itself. A clone gets fresh storage and      initializes normally; the implementation can never be initialized,      so nobody can take ownership of the address the clones point at.

totalSupply().details: Returns the value of tokens in existence.

balanceOf(address).details: Returns the value of tokens owned by `account`.

swapBackThreshold().details: DERIVED FROM THE POOL PRICE, not stored. The real rule is a quote      value - swapBack once the pot is worth      {ArgusConstants-MIN_SWAPBACK_VALUE_USDC6} - and this converts that      into tokens at the current price, floored by the token sanity floor.      Two consequences for anything reading it:      1. It MOVES EVERY BLOCK, because the price does. Comparing         `accumulatedTax()` against a fresh read is correct; caching it is         not. It used to be a storage slot, so a bot that cached it was         previously fine and now is not.      2. It returns `type(uint256).max` when no pool is registered, rather         than reverting, so batch readers do not blow up on a token that         has not graduated.

setMainPool(address).details: Registering early is the whole point: a v3 pool address is      CREATE2-deterministic from (factory, token0, token1, fee), so the      Portal knows it the moment the clone exists, and knowing it is what      lets {_update} block anyone from seeding that pool at a rigged price      ahead of graduation.      Honest limitation: this blocks THE pool, not every conceivable pool.      A rogue pool at a different fee tier is undetectable on-chain - a      pool is just an address. The canonical pool is the one that matters,      because it is the one graduation seeds and the one aggregators route      to.

approve(address,uint256).details: See {IERC20-approve}. NOTE: If `value` is the maximum `uint256`, the allowance is not updated on `transferFrom`. This is semantically equivalent to an infinite approval. Requirements: - `spender` cannot be the zero address.

params.minOutNative18: Caller's own floor on proceeds. Only ever TIGHTENS:        the spot-derived fill floor below still applies in full, so a sized        call can never be used to slip past it. Pass 0 to rely on the        automatic floor alone.

swapBack(uint256,uint256).details: The escape hatch for the one case the automatic cap cannot see.      `pool.liquidity()` reports IN-RANGE liquidity only, so a third-party      concentrated position sitting on the current tick makes the pool look      deeper than it is a few ticks away: the cap sizes a slice against      liquidity that evaporates mid-swap, the 85% floor catches it, and the      no-arg form then has no way to respond - it recomputes the same size      and fails identically forever. That is the same stranded-pot failure      the liquidity cap was added to remove, arriving by a different route.      A caller who can see the book picks a slice that clears the floor.      A caller-sized swap-back deliberately does NOT move the dynamic      threshold or the output-per-token EMA. Two reasons, and the second is      the load-bearing one:      1. §6 compares realised output against a reference for a slice WE         sized. An observation from a slice someone else sized is not a         measurement of the same thing.      2. Without it, anyone could churn the controller for the price of         gas: dust-sized calls return zero proceeds, read as a weak market,         and walk the threshold wherever the griefer wants inside its         clamp. The no-arg path is caller-independent, so it is the only         one allowed to feed the loop.

transfer(address,uint256).details: See {IERC20-transfer}. Requirements: - `to` cannot be the zero address. - the caller must have a balance of at least `value`.

allowance(address,address).details: Returns the remaining number of tokens that `spender` will be allowed to spend on behalf of `owner` through {transferFrom}. This is zero by default. This value changes when {approve} or {transferFrom} are called.

reduceTaxes(uint16,uint16).details: Down-only, and zero is a legal destination: turning the tax off early      is the same promise as letting it expire. `buyTaxBps + sellTaxBps > 0`      is an initialize-time check about picking the right launch mode, not      a floor the creator is trapped above.

transferFrom(address,address,uint256).details: See {IERC20-transferFrom}. Skips emitting an {Approval} event indicating an allowance update. This is not required by the ERC. See {xref-ERC20-_approve-address-address-uint256-bool-}[_approve]. NOTE: Does not update the allowance if the current allowance is the maximum `uint256`. Requirements: - `from` and `to` cannot be the zero address. - `from` must have a balance of at least `value`. - the caller must have allowance for ``from``'s tokens of at least `value`.

uniswapV3SwapCallback(int256,int256,byte.details: Pays the pool for the swap it is mid-way through.      Paying from inside the callback, against a pool this contract called      directly, is a requirement and not a style choice. Arc enforces a      blocklist at runtime, and the two USDC entry points are not      symmetric: `0x3600`'s `transfer` does NOT consult it, while      `transferFrom` DOES, and it checks the SPENDER. Routing swap-back      through approve + SwapRouter02 instead would put this token contract      under a blocklist check on every single swap-back. The direct      `pool.swap()` keeps both legs on `transfer`: the pool pays us by      `transfer`, and we pay it with a plain internal balance move.

initialize((string,string,string,uint256.details: Bundled into a struct rather than taken as eleven arguments because      the flat form is stack-too-deep on 0.8.24 without via-IR, in the      compiler's own ABI decoder.

tokenIsToken0.details: Cached from `pool.token0()` at registration. `swapBack()` needs to      know which side of the pair it is selling before it can pick a swap      direction, a price bound, or read the callback deltas the right way      round.

SHARE_SYNC_GAS.details: Gas ceiling on each {IArgusDividendTracker-setShare}. Sized against the      real implementation's measured cost, not a guess: 2.5k on the      unchanged-share early-out, ~52k median, ~69k for a first-time holder      (three cold SSTOREs plus the one-off staticcall to {mainPool}), and a      ~113k one-time path where the tracker first LEARNS the pool address      and has to un-count a share it had already credited to it. Worst case      those combine, so the cap has to clear ~182k.      Undersizing this is SILENT and permanent: the try/catch swallows the      out-of-gas, the trade succeeds, and that holder's share is simply      never recorded - they earn nothing and `totalShares` is wrong from      then on. {_syncPool} exists to retire the 113k path at launch so the      combined worst case never actually occurs.

_expectedPoolCallback.details: Set immediately before `pool.swap()` and cleared immediately after,      exactly as {PotatoCurvePad} does it. Outside that window every      callback is rejected, so the callback cannot be used to make this      contract pay out its own balance.
